chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Qadisiyyah: Do I go there and complete the prayer or shorten it? He said, 'And how far is it?' I said, 'It is what you saw.' He said, 'Shorten it.'

key_terms.أُتِمُّ: I complete (the four-rak'ah prayer to four rak'ahs).
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: I shorten (the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs).
key_terms.الْقَادِسِيَّةِ: Al-Qadisiyyah, a specific location known for its distance from Kufa, often used as a benchmark for travel distance in fiqh.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer when traveling to Al-Qadisiyyah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for travelers heading to Al-Qadisiyyah, a historically significant region in Iraq. By asking 'How far is it?' and then instructing to shorten the prayer, the Imam establishes that the distance to this location meets the criteria for *safar* (travel), thereby obligating *qasr* (shortening of the four-rak'ah prayers). This highlights the practical application of distance-based rulings in Shia jurisprudence.
